Lemma
[Differentiation under the integral sign] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0283, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-iii:page-0284 1. ch23:23.40\group Supplementary analysis

If $f\in C^1(\mathcal M\times [\alpha ,\omega ])$ and both $\int f\, d\mu $ and $\int \partial _tf\, d\mu $ converge uniformly in $t$, then \[ \frac d{dt}\int _{\mathcal M}f(x,t)\, d\mu (x) =\int _{\mathcal M}\partial _tf(x,t)\, d\mu (x). \]
Proof

\sketch Apply Lemma 5 to $\partial _tf$ and use the fundamental theorem of calculus on each spatial point; uniform convergence permits passage to the spatial integral.

□
